conventions.deletions_are_removals_not_corrections: velocity/loudspeaker/map syn deletions and pull/elevate family deletions remove a misleading entry; they do not claim the removed word is unrelated in all senses.
conventions.pos_tagged_syn: jail/rally syn entries carry the same '(pos.)' suffix format as family entries (e.g. 'prison (n.)'), because vocab_units.syn is a flat TEXT[] with no per-sense column. Question generation must strip the ' (pos.)' suffix before display and must not take a syn token across POS. If integration-2 prefers to keep syn plain, the alternative is to leave jail/rally syn untouched in the DB and enforce POS-split only in the question-generation layer; do NOT silently drop prison/imprison/gathering/mobilise/recover, each is a valid same-POS synonym for one of the headword's senses.

order: import -> apply patches -> validate (re-running the import overwrites these patches, so patches must be re-applied after any import)

patches.queue_policy: Student-end: demote to C2 extension / hidden word; exclude from the daily new-word queue; display the note verbatim when shown. This policy must be implemented in the queue filter layer by integration-2, not by editing cefr/topic/note here.
patches.reason: Sample §4.1: the headword itself is a rare verb form; the upstream note already admits it is rare. Do NOT delete the note. No vocab_units field encodes queue membership, so there is no honest DB field edit for this item.

Sample §4.2: tip says velocity includes direction in physics while speed does not, so listing speed as a plain synonym contradicts the tip. Deleted (the 'near-synonym with annotation' alternative was rejected to keep syn strictly same-meaning).

Sample §4.3: syn mixed POS (noun prison, verb imprison) while the headword is n./v. Split by POS using the family-style suffix, since syn is a flat TEXT[]; both entries are kept because each matches one headword POS.

Sample §4.4: syn mixed POS (noun gathering, verbs mobilise/recover) while the headword is n./v. Split by POS using the family-style suffix; all three entries are kept because each matches one headword POS.

Sample §4.5: speaker is far broader than loudspeaker (also a person speaking, a chair, etc.) and the tip itself warns of this; listing it as a synonym misleads sense-choice questions. Family entry 'speaker (n.)' is untouched because §4.5 only flagged syn.
Sample §4.6: chart mostly means a sea chart / diagram, not an everyday map; at A1 this misleads most. Deleted rather than annotated, to keep A1 syn strictly equivalent.
Sample §4.7: puller is extremely rare and has no teaching value as a family display item.

Sample §4.8: elevator in American English primarily means 'lift', so its link to elevate ('raise') needs an extra hop; showing it as a plain derived word invites rote memorisation of 'elevator = derivation of elevate'. Deleted (the 'annotate as lift' alternative was rejected to keep family strictly derivational).
